errors.text: The segregation chemistry is incorrect: the target mechanism has Au and Cu enriching the surface, whereas the hypothesis places Cu in the core and substitutes Pt as a principal surface-segregating species.

Loss of the smallest particles is attributed primarily to Ostwald ripening and growth of larger particles, while the target identifies Au/Cu surface-shell melting and evaporation, with an overall particle-size reduction.
The proposed approximately 5 nm critical threshold and recovery of sluggish-diffusion stabilization above 20 nm are unsupported and omit the experimentally important activation boundary near 673 K.
The initial synthesis route and structure are misreconstructed: carbothermal shock and a generic homogeneous state replace PLD at 873 K and the FCC multi-twinned/icosahedral initial structure.
